title: Site-to-site VPN and remote-access VPN: when to use each

videos.script: A company has two offices, and people who sometimes work from home. It needs VPNs for both, and they are not the same VPN. {{two}} Between the offices, the tunnel runs from router to router. Nobody logs in, and the till at the branch has no idea it exists. {{till}} You will see that from the till itself. A traceroute to the head office crosses the whole internet in one hop. {{hop}} For people, the tunnel runs from each laptop to the head office. Now the question is who is connecting, and how you know. {{person}} Then the decision every remote-access setup has to make. Does only company traffic go through the tunnel, or everything? {{split}} You will make the same request both ways, and read the web server's log. It saw two different clients. {{log}} Next, two ways a home network gets in the way. Names that the home router cannot answer, and an address range the office shares with the kitchen. {{overlap}} Last, a table for choosing, and a look at what some companies use instead of a VPN for people. {{choose}}
